introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Physics 2 (0780), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2023. Time allowed: three hours.**

Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour, Section II in 30 minutes and Section III in 1 hour. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you must show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators and formulae booklet are allowed.

**Structure of the paper.** SECTION I (headed "One hour 30 minutes" on page 2): questions 1 to 5 are compulsory; in question 6 answer EITHER 6 (a), (b) and (c) OR 6 (d), (e) and (f). SECTION II (40 minutes): DATA ANALYSIS, question 7. SECTION III (50 minutes): OPTIONS - answer any two questions from the four options (Option 1: Energy resources and environmental physics, question 8; Option 2: Communication, question 9; Option 3: Electronics, question 10; Option 4: Medical physics, question 11).

No data sheet is printed in the paper: whenever a constant is needed, the model answer states the value it uses.
enonce_intro_markdown:
Some electrical components are connected together in a circuit energized by $3.00\ \mathrm{V}$ battery as shown in figure 2. The capacitors are initially uncharged. The contact point Z of the switch is closed at point X until the $1.00\times10^{2}\ \mu\mathrm{F}$ capacitor is fully charged. When Z is now moved to make contact with Y, determine

![fig-1](gce-al-physics-2023-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_5_fig_1.png)

figures.legende: Figure 2 : circuit with a 3 V battery, a 1.5 kilohm resistor in series with a 150 microfarad capacitor (branch ending at Y), a milliammeter in series with a 100 microfarad capacitor (branch ending at Z), and the switch contact Z that can touch X or Y.

incertitudes: Question 5 : schéma lu comme suit : Z relié à la branche mA + 100 uF ; en X la pile charge le 100 uF, en Y le 100 uF chargé se décharge dans la branche 1,5 kilo-ohm + 150 uF (pile hors circuit). Cette lecture est la seule cohérente avec l'énoncé (« the 1.00 x 10^2 uF capacitor is fully charged ») ; elle donne 2,00 mA puis 180 uC.

questions.enonce_markdown: The initial current in the circuit.
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Z at X:** the battery charges the $100\ \mu\mathrm{F}$ capacitor to the battery p.d. of $3.00\ \mathrm{V}$, so it stores
$$Q_0 = CV = 100\times10^{-6}\times3.00 = 3.00\times10^{-4}\ \mathrm{C}\ (300\ \mu\mathrm{C}).$$

**Z moved to Y:** the battery is now disconnected. The charged $100\ \mu\mathrm{F}$ capacitor is connected in a closed loop with the $1.5\ \mathrm{k\Omega}$ resistor and the **uncharged** $150\ \mu\mathrm{F}$ capacitor (the milliammeter has negligible resistance). At the first instant the $150\ \mu\mathrm{F}$ capacitor has no p.d. across it, so the whole $3.00\ \mathrm{V}$ of the charged capacitor appears across the resistor:

$$I_0 = \frac{V}{R} = \frac{3.00}{1.5\times10^{3}} = 2.00\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{A}$$

**Initial current = 2.00 mA** (it then decays as the $150\ \mu\mathrm{F}$ capacitor charges).

questions.enonce_markdown: The maximum charge that will be stored in the $150\ \mu\mathrm{F}$ capacitor.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The charge of $Q_0 = 300\ \mu\mathrm{C}$ is shared between the two capacitors: charge is conserved, so
$$Q_1 + Q_2 = Q_0 = 300\ \mu\mathrm{C}.$$

The current stops when there is no p.d. across the resistor, so the two capacitor p.d.s are then equal and opposing round the loop:
$$\frac{Q_1}{C_1} = \frac{Q_2}{C_2}\quad\Rightarrow\quad \frac{300 - Q_2}{100} = \frac{Q_2}{150}.$$

$$150(300 - Q_2) = 100\,Q_2 \Rightarrow Q_2 = \frac{150}{250}\times300 = 180\ \mu\mathrm{C}$$

Final common p.d. $= \dfrac{180}{150} = 1.20\ \mathrm{V}$ (and the $100\ \mu\mathrm{F}$ capacitor keeps $120\ \mu\mathrm{C}$, since $100\times1.20 = 120$).

**Maximum charge on the $150\ \mu\mathrm{F}$ capacitor $= 180\ \mu\mathrm{C} = 1.8\times10^{-4}\ \mathrm{C}$.**
